author: maintainer-agent

patch.value:
## Problem
Merge safety was delivered as a program and closed. The artifact surface has grown since. The failure mode is quiet: a new file class ships without a merge driver entry, the default line-based driver applies, and two agents' work corrupts on merge — visible only after the fact.

## Approach
Property-based conformance rather than example tests. Generate branch divergence randomly, merge in random orders, and assert algebraic properties: convergence, commutativity of independent merges, and history union completeness. Fence coverage becomes a derived assertion, not a checklist someone must remember to update.

## Relationship to shipped work
Consumes the shipped merge drivers, history union and reanchoring, storage integrity validation, and the fence. Adds the continuous proof those pieces lack. Shares the seeded-schedule infrastructure with the deterministic simulation harness rather than duplicating it.

## Boundary
Not a new merge algorithm. Contradictory-edit policy is documented behaviour to assert, not to redesign here.
Continuous multi-branch merge conformance: randomized N-branch divergence and merge property suite with a zero-conflict acceptance bar

The suite generates randomized divergent branches covering create, update, close, annotate, dependency edit, schema change, and config change; Merges are asserted order-independent: merging the same branch set in different orders converges to the same state; Every tracked artifact class is covered by the fence, and a new unfenced artifact class fails the suite rather than silently merging with the default driver; History union preserves every entry from every branch with no cross-author loss and a verifying chain after reanchor; Conflict count is asserted at zero for non-contradictory concurrent edits, and contradictory edits produce a deterministic, documented resolution
Agents working the same workspace on different branches merge without conflict or loss, provably and continuously

The merge-safety program shipped field-aware drivers, history union, and reanchoring, and then closed. Nothing continuously proves those drivers still hold as new artifact classes are added — and new artifact classes keep being added.
Keeps the central multi-agent promise true as the storage surface grows, instead of true as of the day the merge program closed.
A property suite generates N divergent branches with randomized mutation mixes, merges them in randomized orders, and asserts convergence, zero conflicts, and full history union.

Since the merge program closed, new tracked artifact classes appeared (transaction journals, relationship event streams, durable graph index). Each is a candidate fence gap, and the fence-completeness work already identified that pattern once.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
First live end-to-end run of this suite's core scenario against the shipped 2026.7.25 build, so the zero-conflict acceptance bar has a measured starting point. Throwaway git repository, pm merge install applied, base commit with a two-entry stream, then two branches each adding three entries to the same item, then git merge.

Properties that already hold — record these as the baseline the suite must keep, not as work:
- Zero conflict markers anywhere under .agents/pm. The only conflicts git reported were in my sandbox's PM_GLOBAL_PATH telemetry files, which I had placed inside the repository; no tracked pm artifact conflicted.
- History union is complete and loses no author: 2 shared + 3 + 3 = 8 entries, ops create update comment_add update note_add comment_add update learning_add.
- Field-aware convergence keeps both branches' non-contradictory edits: status in_progress from branch A and priority 1 from branch B in the same merged item.
- Every annotation class survives from both sides: 2 comments, 1 note, 1 learning.
- Point-in-time addressing of pre-divergence versions is stable across the merge: pm get --at 2 returns the identical state before and after.

The property that does not hold is the verifying chain after reanchor. Post-merge, pm history <id> --verify returns ok false with verify_failed:current_item_hash_mismatch (latest_after_hash f0dfb167..., current_item_hash 917a2941..., current_matches_latest false); pm validate reports validate_history_drift_hash_mismatches:1 with history_drift warn and overall ok true; and pm history-repair --dry-run reports chain_drift_before false with entries_rehashed 0, correctly declining because the chain itself verifies. The gap is that no entry describes the merged field set, so there is nothing to re-anchor to. The write-side primitive is filed as pm-9j2r3b; this suite's fourth acceptance clause is the property that proves it.
